top_choice_rationale: P001 credits Katori and Ye for the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock and its realization at the 10^-18 level. The magic-wavelength condition lets many neutral atoms be held in the Lamb-Dicke regime and interrogated in parallel, a distinct step from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. The result is mature and reproduced by several laboratories, and the two-name allocation matches the invention-plus-realization record. The omission of Lemonde, Takamoto and the Sr and Yb groups is a real limitation, but the citation wording bounds the claim. I still regard B008 as the larger idea, but its credit problem (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) is unresolved, and it is not on the slate, so a well-scoped award is better than no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my electronic-structure and magnetism work is adjacent to B008 and B051, neither of which is on the slate, and I have no documented tie to Katori or Ye.
